lead.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing says it may soon hit its own threshold for self-improving AI
lead.summary: Buried in Monday's revised S-1A, next to the soaring revenue and expenses, Anthropic added new risk factors: it has already used AI to build models whose leaps in capability it didn't recognise at the time, and it may soon meet its internal definition of recursive self-improvement. No current model is designated as past that line, it says, and it doesn't expect Claude to safely design its own successors without meaningful human oversight. It's now weighing Responsible Scaling Policy changes to keep humans in control of frontier model development.

news.headline: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum for $115B to own the lasers inside AI data centres
news.summary: An all-stock deal: 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, about a 24% premium, leaving Marvell holders with 67%. Lumentum makes optics that move data between AI chips as light instead of over copper. Closing is expected in the first half of 2028.

news.headline: Trajectory raises $45M so domain experts can keep retraining open models without an ML team
news.summary: The 18-person Stanford spin-out (Sequoia-led Series A, $300M valuation) does continual learning: connect your app, collect feedback, and it post-trains an open-source model on it. Harvey and Rogo already use it, and the platform is now public.

news.headline: Grok Bot users wake up to maxed-out weekly limits, and Musk says it's on purpose
news.summary: Over the weekend some users saw usage jump from 50% to 100% overnight. Musk replied on X that serving costs were unsustainably high relative to revenue. One more sign this week that flat-rate agent plans are being repriced.

news.headline: Finland's national risk assessment: relying on a few foreign AI vendors could expose us to pressure
news.summary: The interior ministry's updated assessment (24 risks, roughly a five-year view) flags AI both as a cyberattack accelerator and as a dependency risk, since key models and clouds come from a handful of foreign firms. Data centres are named as possible terror targets.
